title: Change
description: What a later capture of a primary source showed about a row the register had already published, or a correction a person made to one, citing the evidence. The published row stays exactly as published, unless a person's correction moves one of its facts; then this row keeps what the fact was (CHARTER Vow V; INVARIANTS §14). The adapter (src/adapters/house-fd/build.py) writes one where a capture later than the one a row was read from shows it otherwise; tools/correct.py writes a person's correction. Either way the bytes of the capture it cites are kept in data/captures/sha256/, named by their SHA-256, so the change can be checked from the repository alone once the source serves something else, except a filed document (a PDF), which is never kept: a filed document can carry the names of private people, and a kept copy would outlast the Clerk's withdrawal or redaction of it (EVIDENCE.md §7), so a document is cited by its URL, the time it was read and its SHA-256, and a replaced one records which of its rows read otherwise, never what they say. A change row never changes and is never removed: data/changes.ndjson only grows at its end. It carries the frame, because a change row names a person's row and may be read without the page.

id.description: ch:<change>:<row id>[:<field>]:<the capture's retrieved_at>. One change per row, kind, field and capture.

row_id.description: The id of the published row the change is about.

rows.description: Which of the register's files holds that row.

change.description: not listed: the capture does not list the row (the Clerk's roster no longer lists the officeholder, or the index the filing); the source does not say why. listed again: a later capture lists a row an earlier one did not. read otherwise: the capture, as the register reads it, gives one of the row's facts another value (`field`, `was`, `now`); the row keeps the value it was published with. replaced: the source serves other bytes for a filing's document, and they read otherwise (`differs`); the rows read from the first bytes are kept as published, and neither file is kept. corrected: a person moved one of the row's facts, or recorded that it stands, or recorded how many rows a report's own bytes list (`field` transactions), citing the evidence (`because`, `kind`, `decided_by`, `decided_at`).

field.description: The fact the change is about, as a path into the row (filed_at, officeholder_id, source.content_hash). On read otherwise, replaced and corrected. On a correction of a filing, `transactions` is the number of rows the report's bytes list, which the maintainer's decision accepts where a later reading of the very bytes the rows were published from finds more; the adapter adds no such row without it.

was.description: The value the published row carries for the field; for a correction, the value it carried before. A correction of a transaction's asset or notes carries `was_sha256` instead.

was_sha256.description: On a correction of a transaction's asset or notes, the text the filer wrote: the SHA-256 of the value it carried, hashed as canonical JSON (json.dumps with sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, the default separators), in place of the value. So a line a filer has the Clerk remove, a private person's name among them, is not in the register's changes; the build that published the line carries it still, as every sealed build stays in the repository's history (LIMITATIONS.md §9; the Council's third reading of S.1b, Seat B, and its fourth, Seats B, E and G). A correction's `now` is the text as corrected, in plain.

differs.description: On replaced: which rows of the document read otherwise than the rows published from it, by id and field name, never by value. Empty when a later file reads as the rows published.

row.description: A transaction's id, or the filing's, for its header.

fields.description: The facts a published row carries that this file gives another value.

only_in.description: A row one file lists and the other does not.

header.description: What the document's own header prints that refuses the row's attribution (a Filing ID, a seat, a filer status).

now.description: The value the capture gives, or the value a correction sets. Equal to `was` when the source reads as published again, or when a person records that the published value stands.

kind.description: A correction's kind: the source now states the fact otherwise (source), or the register read or joined it wrongly (register).

because.description: A correction's reason, in one sentence, naming what the evidence shows.

decided_by.description: Who made the correction, by role.

decided_at.description: When the correction was made, UTC.

before.description: When the register last built from a capture of the same source before this one, UTC. The change fell between the two reads; the register does not know when, or why.

before_content_hash.description: The SHA-256 of the bytes of that earlier read. The register keeps them in data/captures/sha256/ only where a change row or a closed year cites them.

entry_sha256.description: On read otherwise: the SHA-256 of the row's own entry in the capture, found without the XML parser. A change is recorded only where the row's entry changed since the register last read it; a later capture whose entry has this same hash says nothing new about the row.

capture.description: The capture that shows the change, or the evidence a correction cites: where it was read, when (UTC), and the SHA-256 of the bytes, which the register keeps at data/captures/sha256/<content_hash> with the capture's own extension, unless they are a filed document (a PDF), which it never keeps.

build.description: The build the row was first sealed in, as tools/seal.py stamps it.

frame.const: Presence in the register is not evidence of wrongdoing.
frame.description: The register's frame, on the row, because the row can travel without the page.

examples.frame: Presence in the register is not evidence of wrongdoing.
Presence in the register is not evidence of wrongdoing.
